results.title: How to Create a Listing
results.body:
Before you can create a listing, you must register as a seller. Review our Seller Policy to make sure your items fit into Etsy’s handmade, vintage, or craft supply categories.

  1. Sign in and go to Shop Manager.
  2. Select Listings.
  3. Select Add a listing.
  4. Fill in the relevant information in the listing creation form. 
  5. When you’re finished, select Publish. The listing is now live in your shop.

  1. Go to Listings. 
  2. Select + in the top right corner and choose Copy an existing listing or Start from scratch. 
  3. Select a category that best describes your listing. If you don’t see a good match, choose Select a different category to see more options. 
  4. Upload photos and/or videos that show off your item. You’ll be able to edit your uploads later in the process. 
  5. Enter relevant and required information for your listing. Select Next and Back to navigate between sections.
  6. When finished, select Publish.

Once published, it may take up to 48 hours for your listing to appear in Etsy search results and categories.

If you’d rather save the listing for later, select Save as Draft instead. 

Learn how to copy a listing to create multiple listings at once. 

There are 7 tabs in the listing form you must fill out before you can publish.

Jump to a section:

  • Photo & video
  • Category
  • Item details
  • Item options
  • Pricing & shipping
  • How it's made
  • Settings

Photo & video

You can add up to 20 photos and 2 videos that are 5-15 seconds in length to each listing. Select Edit to adjust the image thumbnail, crop the photo to the aspect ratio of your choosing, or delete the photo. Select Apply when finished. Learn about best practices for images in your Etsy shop.

Category

Based on the photos and/or videos you provided, this section will be prefilled. Confirm the selections are correct, and make updates as needed.

  • Find a category: The category determines which sections of Etsy’s marketplace your item appears in. Type the category of your item into the search bar, then under Results, select the option that is the closest match for what you’re listing.
  • What type of item is it?: Select whether you’re listing a physical item or digital files.
  • When was it made?: Select when you made the item you’re selling.

Item details

This is what shoppers see when browsing for items on Etsy, so be sure to follow best practices for getting your items found in search. From here you can add:

  • Title: A listing’s title can be up to 140 characters long. Consider using less than 15 words when including the traits that make your item special. Clearly state what the item is and any key details. Avoid repetition as well as subjective words (for example, “perfect”). There’s no need to add information about price or shipping to your title. Only include holidays, special occasions, or recipient types if they’re essential to what the item is (for example, “Halloween costume”). 
  • Your listing's unique URL is based on the title you enter when you first publish the listing. Once you've published the listing, the URL won’t change again, even if you edit the title later. If you make major changes to your listing, consider creating a new listing so the URL better reflects what's being sold.
  • Digital files: Add up to 5 files for buyers to download when purchasing a digital item from your shop. This section only appears if you have indicated you are listing digital files.
  • Description: Describe the details of your item so buyers know what they’re getting. When possible, include keywords buyers would use when searching for an item like this. Learn about best practices for listing descriptions.

Item options

  • Variations: Add variations to your listing if you’d like to offer different options for the item, like size or color. You’ll only be able to add variations to an item once you’ve selected a category for the item in the Details section. Variations are unavailable for digital listings. Learn how to add variations to your listings. 
  • Personalization: Select Add Personalization if you want to offer the ability to customize your item. Then, add in any personalization instructions you want buyers to see, set a limit on the number of characters a buyer can request when customizing the item, and select if you want to make personalization optional or mandatory for this item. Learn more about personalization.
  • Attributes: Give details about the qualities of the item, such as the color, material, size dimensions, etc. The attributes listed under this section will change depending on the category you selected. Learn more about how to use attributes for your listings.
  • Tags: Add up to 13 tags that describe your item. Try to include keywords buyers would use when searching for an item like this. This helps your item appear in shoppers’ search results. Learn how using tags can help you get found in search.

Pricing & shipping

Price and inventory

  • Price: Set the amount buyers will pay for your item here. The price will appear in your preferred currency. When you enter a price on a listing, a profit estimate appears. This can be either a single price or a range, depending on your variation settings. Select the dropdown to see more details.
  • Quantity: Add the amount of the item you have for sale. Learn more about how item quantity works with listing fees.
  • SKU: Create a custom SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) number for the item to help keep track of your inventory.

Shipping, processing, and returns

Apply accurate processing and shipping information to your listings so buyers have realistic expectations on when the order will arrive. If the listing is for a digital item, buyers will download the files you uploaded immediately after purchase. 

  1. While creating your listing, go to Processing profile.
  2. Select Create.
  3. Select if your item is Made to order or Ready to ship.
  4. Choose the processing time from the How much processing time do you need? dropdown.
  5. Select Apply.

  1. While creating your listing, go to Processing and shipping and select Processing profile.
  2. Select Create new.
  3. Select if your item is Made to order or Ready to ship.
  4. Choose a time from the Processing time dropdown.
  5. Select Save.

If you already have processing profiles, Etsy will pre-fill this section for you. 

  1. Go to Processing profile.
  2. Select Change profile. 
  3. Select Apply on the processing profile you wish to use, or select Create new to add another.

  1. Go to Processing and shipping.
  2. Go to Processing profile and select the pencil icon to edit. 
  3. Select the processing profile you wish to apply and select Save. To add a new processing profile, select Create new.

Learn more about processing profiles.

  1. In the Shipping option section, choose Select Profile. 
  2. Choose one of your existing shipping profiles and select Apply or fill in the required information to create a new shipping option. For calculated shipping, you must enter the item weight and item size (when packed).
  3. If the item will be sent with an international shipping label, you can enter the Tariff Number to prefill a customs form.

Select Change if you need to apply a different shipping profile to your listing. You can also select the three dots next to a shipping profile to Edit or Duplicate it.

GPSR manufacturer and safety information

If you’re a “trader” selling to European Economic Area (EEA) states or Northern Ireland (NI), you may need to include manufacturer and safety information to comply with the General Product Safety Regulation (GPSR). 

If you’re listing a physical item, you can also provide Customs information that is used to prefill a customs form when you purchase an international shipping label on Etsy.

How it's made

These are the most basic aspects of your listing, including who made the item, what it is, and when it was made. Add any production partners involved in the creation of this item.

Settings

Adjust settings to how your listing appears and how it will renew.

  • Shop section: Select which of your shop sections you want the listing displayed in or create a new one. Learn more about how to organize your listings with shop sections.
  • Feature this listing: Switch the toggle button on to display the listing at the top of your shop’s homepage.
  • Renewal options: Choose if you want your listings to automatically renew after they expire, or if you’d rather renew them manually. See our policy page to learn more about listing fees.

Questions about listings?

Ask the Community

You can edit all parts of a listing at any time. There's no cost to edit a listing.

If you’re having trouble creating or editing listings, select an issue to learn how to resolve it:

If you find your listing isn’t renewing properly, or says it Needs Review when you are making edits, you’ll need to clarify some parts of your shipping preferences. 

Etsy requires sellers from all origin countries to provide an estimated delivery date to save a shipping profile and listing. 

For each listing, you will need to have the following information completely filled out:

  • Domestic shipping service
    • If Other is selected, you must provide a delivery time.
       
  • Cross-border shipping service
    • If Other is selected, you must provide a delivery time.
    • Cross-border services will be required of all sellers in all countries who ship internationally.
  • If you offer shipping upgrades, shipping service or delivery time.
  • Origin ZIP/postal code/postcode/PIN, which the ioptem is shipping from
  • A processing time to indicate how long you need to get an order ready and handed off to your shipping carrier. Learn how to set a processing time.

You are required to add the above information to listings/shipping profiles whenever you:

  • Create a new listing
  • Duplicate a listing
  • Edit an existing listing
  • Create a new shared or custom shipping profile
  • Duplicate a shipping profile
  • Edit an existing shipping profile

Your image may be too small or too large

We recommend your images be at least 2000 pixels wide. You may want to use image editing software to resize your images before uploading them to Etsy.

Files bigger than 300k may time out, especially on a slower internet connection. Try using a smaller file or compressing your file to reduce its size.

If you are seeing the error message “Listings look best with photos at least 2000 pixels wide”

This error appears when the images uploaded to a listing are less than 2000 pixels wide. While this error is only a suggestion and you should be able to continue publishing, having your listing images be at least 2000 pixels wide will result in better quality images for buyers.

If you’re experiencing a different issue with image uploads, check the steps in this Help Center article.

You can create a new variation type by selecting Create a new variation from the Add or Edit variations popup window. However, buyers won’t be able to filter their Etsy search results based on custom variations.

For example, if you want to offer a unisex size variation, you can choose Create a new variation and type in “Size.”

This is normal, and you'll see the variations and price differences you added when you publish your listing. Try publishing your listing. You can see how buyers can interact with variations from the published listing.

If you’re a seller outside the US and India, you can set up a different listing price for orders shipping within your country and orders shipping outside your country. Learn more to set up domestic & global pricing.

Everything listed for sale on Etsy must be handmade, vintage, or a craft supply. Items sold on Etsy must also follow our Prohibited Items Policy.

Handmade items

Handmade items are items that are made and/or designed by you, the seller. If you sell handmade items, you must:

  • Physically make or create the original designs for your items.
  • Include each person involved in making your items or running your business in the About section of your shop. If you work with a production partner, you must disclose that production partner in your relevant listings.
  • Use your own photographs in your listings.

Read our full Handmade Policy.

Vintage items

Vintage items must be at least 20 years old. Newer, vintage-style, or collectible items aren’t allowed in this category.

Learn more about selling vintage items on Etsy.

Craft supplies

Craft supplies on Etsy are tools, ingredients, or materials whose primary purpose is for use in the creation of an item or special occasion. Craft supplies may be handmade, commercial, or vintage. Party supplies may also be sold as craft supplies.

Learn about what can be sold as a craft supply.

If your listing was removed by Etsy for a violation of Etsy’s policies, check your email inbox for a message from Etsy. In the email you received about this listing(s), you’ll be told the reason it was removed.

If you’re unable to locate an email about your listing:

  • Make sure you’re using the email address registered with the shop that the listing was associated with
  • Check your spam or junk mail

Also be sure to review Etsy’s policies to ensure that your items can be listed on our marketplace. 

You can deactivate or delete a listing from your Listings page. Check the box next to the listing, then choose Deactivate or Delete. If you deactivate a listing, you can reactivate it later. If you delete a listing, it is permanently deleted.

  • Quantity

results.title: How to Share to Social Media from Your Shop
results.body:
Social media is a powerful marketing tool that can help you promote your products, reach potential new customers, and entice existing customers to buy again. 

Tips for using social media as a marketing tool:

  • Post regularly so followers come to expect and look forward to your posts. Create a schedule so you avoid large breaks between posts.
  • Respond to comments to make your customers part of the conversation.
  • Share a mix of posts that promote your products, showcase your process and inspiration, and provide value to your followers.
  • Tailor your posts to each channel to avoid overwhelming your followers with similar content.

How to create a social media post on Etsy

From the Social media section in your shop, you can quickly promote your shop and share important updates to sites like Facebook, Instagram, and X (formerly Twitter).

There are six types of posts you can create through Etsy:

  • Latest listings you’ve added (up to 25 of your most recent listings) 
  • Recent milestones successes, like your shop’s anniversary
  • Current or upcoming sales and coupons 
  • 5-star reviews 
  • Items you’ve favorited 

To create a social media post on Etsy.com:

  1. Go to Shop Manager.
  2. Choose Marketing.
  3. Choose Social Media.
  4. Choose Social accounts to connect an account.
  5. When you’re ready to create a post, select Create post.
  6. Select the type of post you want to create.
  7. Choose Next.
  8. Add images and a caption.
  9. Select the networks you want to share your post with.
  10. Choose Post and continue.
  11. Choose Done

To create a social media post on the Etsy Seller app:

  1. Select More on the navigation bar.
  2. Under Marketing, select Social media.
  3. Select which listing you want to share, which are filtered by Newest, Most favorites, Least views, and Most views.
  4. Select Share listing.
  5. Choose one image or video from your listing to share.
  6. Select Next. 
  7. Select Share. This will save your listing link to your device's clipboard. 
  8. Choose which social media account you want to share your listing on. 
  9. Finish posting your listing. Remember to include the listing link you copied earlier. 

Buyers can buy the items that are tagged in the photos by clicking on the orange price tag or clicking through the listing image on the right of the photo.

To learn more about marketing your Etsy shop, read the Ultimate Guide to Marketing.

results.name: How Etsy's Offsite Ads Work
results.title: How Etsy's Offsite Ads Work
results.body:
Quick Answer

Etsy’s Offsite Ads program promotes your listings across external sites like search engines, social media, and partner networks. You only pay a fee when a buyer clicks an ad and makes a purchase from your shop within 30 days.

In this article:

  • How do Offsite Ads work?
  • How do Offsite Ads fees and enrollment work?
  • When are my orders attributed to Offsite Ads?
  • Where does Etsy advertise?
  • How can I track my Offsite Ads performance?
  • Frequently asked questions
  • Additional resources

How do Offsite Ads work?

You don’t need to take any steps to be eligible for Offsite Ads. Etsy works with partner sites and networks to promote your listings on their pages. Etsy shares listing data (title, images, descriptions, etc.) with ad platforms, and their algorithms match your listing to relevant shoppers.

You can’t choose which listings are advertised. Instead, listings are advertised based on what performs best on each channel. Your listings may be automatically advertised at Etsy’s discretion. To increase the chance of your listings being advertised, improve the quality of your listings. 

How do Offsite Ads fees and enrollment work?

Your Offsite Ads fee rate and enrollment status are based on your shop’s revenue within any consecutive 365-day period:

If you’re a seller with a shop currency other than USD, your revenue total is calculated from your order amounts converted to USD with the currency exchange rates Etsy used at the time that the sale was processed.

How do I opt out of Offsite Ads?

If your shop has never made $10,000 USD or more in any consecutive 365-day period, you can opt out of Offsite Ads. 

  1. On Etsy.com, choose Shop Manager.
  2. Select Settings.
  3. Select Offsite Ads.
  4. Choose Opt out of Offsite Ads.
  5. Confirm that you want Etsy to Opt out of Offsite Ads.

If you want to re-enroll in Offsite Ads, visit the Offsite Ads page and choose Turn on Offsite Ads.

When are my orders attributed to Offsite Ads?

Orders are attributed to Offsite Ads when a buyer clicks on an ad and completes a purchase from your shop within 30 days. If the buyer’s final click before purchasing is through an Etsy Ad instead, only the Etsy Ads fee will apply.

You’re only charged an Offsite Ads fee when a click results in a purchase, there’s no fee if the buyer doesn’t buy anything. A single ad click can lead to multiple attributed orders, so if a buyer makes separate purchases within that 30-day window, each order may incur an Offsite Ads fee.

The Offsite Ads fee for any individual order will never exceed $100 USD, regardless of the order total.

Where does Etsy advertise?

Etsy advertises your listings across search engines, social media platforms, partner sites, and the Google Display Network. These partners may change over time.

Etsy Offsite Ads may appear in the search engines results, platforms, partners and social media sites such as:

  • Google
  • Facebook
  • Instagram
  • Pinterest
  • Bing
  • Etsy Publishing Partner Sites
  • Google Display Network

Learn more and view privacy policies in the Offsite Ad Channels list. 

An Etsy Publishing Partner is a site that offers curated shopping catalogs where Offsite Ads listings may appear. These partners feature curated shopping content where your listings may be promoted.

  • Buzzfeed
  • Martha Stewart
  • Real Simple
  • MyWedding
  • Better Homes and Gardens
  • Lyst
  • Shape

Google Display Network (GDN) lets Etsy advertise to targeted audiences across over 2 million sites. This includes platforms like YouTube, Zillow, Gmail, and Weather.com, reaching users even when they aren’t actively searching. Placements may shift weekly based on user behavior.

How can I track my Offsite Ads performance?

Track stats and performance data, such as revenue, fees, clicks, and ad traffic, through the Offsite Ads dashboard. 

  1. Sign in and go to Shop Manager.
  2. Select Marketing.
  3. Select Offsite Ads.

  • See which search terms and listings drive traffic, then update your titles, tags, and descriptions to better match what buyers are searching for.
  • Identify items that perform well through Offsite Ads and prioritize inventory or production for those items.
  • Look for patterns in clicks and sales so you can plan for seasonal demand or emerging buyer interests.
  • Identify listings that get traffic but not sales and test new photos, pricing, or promotions.
  • See how much of your sales come from Offsite Ads and use that context to guide pricing and margins.

You can also track traffic and visits from Offsite Ads even when they don’t lead to a sale. Since you’re only charged when a purchase is made, this data can help you understand buyer interest and optimize your shop.

Frequently asked questions

You’re only charged when a buyer clicks an Offsite Ad and completes a purchase from your shop within 30 days. You can see which orders are attributed to Offsite Ads in your Offsite Ads dashboard in Shop Manager.

No, listings are advertised based on what performs best on each channel. To increase the chance of your listings being advertised, improve the quality of your listings.

A single ad click can lead to multiple purchases within 30 days. Each order placed in that window may incur an Offsite Ads fee.

No, Offsite Ads don’t have a budget setting. You’re only charged when a sale is made, and fees are capped at $100 USD per order.

If your shop has made $10,000 USD or more in any consecutive 365-day period, participation in Offsite Ads is required.

Additional resources

  • Offsite Ad Channels list
  • Fees & Payments Policy
  • Advertising & Marketing Policy
  • The Essentials of Online Advertising
  • How to Set Up and Manage an Etsy Ads Campaign

Etsy advertises listings throughout the web, including in search engine results and social media apps like Facebook. Etsy offers this service with no upfront costs to you: you only pay an advertising fee when you make a sale.

If you make a sale from one of Etsy’s Offsite Ads, you’ll pay an advertising fee for that order.

Your Offsite Ads fee rate is based on your shop’s revenue within any consecutive 365-day period:

  • If your shop has always made less than $10,000 USD in any consecutive 365 day period, you’ll be charged a 15% fee on the order total for an order attributed to an Offsite Ad.
  • If your shop has made $10,000 USD or more in any consecutive 365 day period, you’ll get a discounted fee of 12%. 

The Offsite Ads fee will never exceed $100 USD, regardless of the order total for an order attributed to an Offsite Ad.

If you’re a seller with a shop currency other than USD, your revenue total is calculated from your order amounts converted to USD with the currency exchange rates Etsy used at the time that the sale was processed.

If a buyer clicks through an offsite ad promoting one of your listings and then purchases from your shop within 30 days, that order will be attributed to the ad.

You’re only charged when a shopper clicks on an ad for one of your listings and purchases from your shop. If a shopper clicks on an ad for your item but doesn’t make a purchase, you don’t pay a fee.

All sellers are automatically enrolled in Offsite Ads. Some sellers will be able to choose whether to participate.

Your eligibility to opt out of Offsite Ads is based on your shop’s revenue within any consecutive 365-day period:

  • If you made $10,000 USD or more on Etsy in any 365-day period, you’ll benefit most from offsite advertising. You’ll be required to participate for the lifetime of your shop and you’ll get a discounted advertising fee.
  • If you've always made less than $10,000 USD on Etsy in any 365-day period, Offsite Ads are optional. However, if you choose to use this service, you’ll get advertising run by our team of experts without any upfront investment, which is a great opportunity to grow your business.

We’ll take a look at your sales each month. Once you’ve made $10,000 USD or more in a 365 day period, you’ll be required to participate in Offsite Ads from then onwards. 

To opt-out of Offsite Ads:

  1. On Etsy.com, click Shop Manager.
  2. Click Settings.
  3. Click Offsite Ads.
  4. Click Opt out of Offsite Ads.
  5. Confirm that you want to Opt out of Offsite Ads.

If you ever want to re-enroll in Offsite Ads, visit the Offsite Ads page and click Turn on Offsite Ads.

results.title: How to Manage Your Pattern Blog
results.body:
With Pattern's blog feature, you can create and share content that tells the story of your business while keeping your buyers informed on any new updates in your shop.

You must own or have permission to use the content that you upload to your Pattern blog.

Jump to a section:

  • How to get your blog set up
  • How to publish and manage your posts
  • How to enable blog comments
  • How visitors see your blog
  • How to track blog performance
  • How to deactivate your blog

How to get your blog set up

To begin the setup process for your blog: 

  1. Go to your Pattern Dashboard. 
  2.  Select the Blog tab, then the Let’s go button.
  3. A sample blog post will be displayed for your reference. Select the title to learn more about available formatting and content options within posts. Delete the draft post when you’re ready, or keep it around to reference.
  4. Select the New Post button at the top of the page to draft your first blog post. From here, you can customize your title, content, featured image, and excerpt.

Title and content

The title of your post plays an important part in your Pattern site's SEO (Search Engine Optimization).

Try to make your title as specific as possible so that it accurately describes the subject of the post. For example, “New Products & Holiday Market Schedule” is more specific than a broad title like “Shop Updates.”

The Content section is where you'll draft and customize content for your post. The toolbar at the top of this section allows you to format your text in:

  • Bold
  • Italics
  • Underline
  • Primary and secondary headings
  • Bulleted lists and numbered lists
  • Hyperlinks

You also have the option to upload images or embed videos from YouTube or Vimeo. To learn more about embedding videos into your blog, check out these step-by-step guides by YouTube and Vimeo.

Featured image and excerpt

These sections are what readers will see on your main blog page before clicking to read the entire post. The featured image displays at the top of your post, and an excerpt briefly summarizing the subject of your post will display below your title.

Excerpts won't appear on this page if you're using the Zephyr theme.

If you choose to not include an image or excerpt, we'll only display your blog post title with a Continue reading link.

What is the maximum image size for blog posts? 

The recommended size for blog post images is 2000px for the longest side of the image, and a resolution of 72PPI. 

Images larger than 1MB in file size may not finish uploading, especially on a slower internet connection. If you're finding that your photo uploads are taking longer than normal (or not successfully uploading), we would recommend downsizing your images and uploading them again.

How to publish and manage your posts

Once you're done composing your post, select Preview to see how it will appear on your site. If you'd like to publish it later, choose Save as Draft. When you're ready to make your post live, select Publish.

To edit a post, go back to the Blog section of your Pattern Dashboard and select title of the post you’d like to edit.

Once you've made changes, you can choose to preview, save as draft, or publish. To cancel the change, select Back to posts at the top of the screen and your edits will be discarded.

To delete a post, go to the Blog section of your Pattern Dashboard to view all of your blog posts. Locate the post you'd like to delete and click the X to the right of the title. Confirm by selecting Delete Post .

Once a post has been deleted, it can't be recovered.

How to enable blog comments

To create more engagement with your blog, give readers the option to comment on your posts through Disqus. This is where you'll manage all of your comment settings for your Pattern blog, and it's free to create an account.

If you choose to enable Disqus, you’ll have the option to turn comments off for specific posts. Use the On / Off toggle under the Excerpt area on the blog post compose screen. This setting defaults to On for new posts.

Learn how to enable comments for your blog.

How visitors see your blog

Once you activate your blog and publish a post, visitors on your Pattern site will see a blog heading in the navigation menu for your site. This link will take them to your full blog, which displays the 10 most recent posts per page.

The location of your blog icon will vary based on the theme you're using.

Visitors will see a preview of each post which displays the title, excerpt, and featured image. They can read the full blog post by selecting the title or the Continue Reading link.

Each blog post also has a unique URL so you can share and promote individual posts with others. Select the post you want to share and copy the entire URL.

How to track blog performance

Your Stats provide a breakdown of blog views and views from individual posts. This will display in the Pages viewed section of your Stats.

If you have Google Analytics enabled for your Pattern site, blog stats will appear there as well. This Help article explains how to set up Google Analytics for Pattern.

To learn more, check out our Pattern Stats Guide.

How to deactivate your blog

From the Blog section of your Pattern Dashboard, select Archive blog at the bottom of the management page. Your blog will be removed from your Pattern site, but your posts will be saved in your dashboard in case you want to reactivate it later.

To turn your blog back on, go to Reactivate your blog at the top of the Blog management page.

results.name: How to Edit a Listing
results.title: How to Edit a Listing
results.body:
Quick answer

To edit a listing, go to your Listings page in Shop Manager or the Etsy Seller app and select a listing image.

You can edit any part of a listing at any time. There's no cost to edit a listing.

Your listing will be available to shoppers while you're editing. If you want to hide a listing while making changes, you can temporarily deactivate it.

Certain aspects of your listings can be bulk edited, if you'd like to edit the same part of multiple listings at once.

Include clear, high-quality images of your item in your listings. Listings with primary images that are too dark, are low quality, are part of photo-collages, or that have too few images may result in your listing appearing lower in search results. You can see if any of your listings need improvements from your Etsy search visibility tab.

How to edit a listing on the Listings page

You can edit every part of the listing from your Listings page. 

If you have lots of listings, you can use the Search by title field to make it easier to find the listing you want to edit.

If you can't find your listing, check your Inactive listings. Learn why listings might be missing.

  1. Sign in and go to Shop Manager. 
  2. Select Listings.
  3. Select the listing you wish to edit. 
  4. Make your changes. When finished, select Publish changes.

  1. Sign in and go to Listings.
  2. Select the listing you wish to edit.
  3. Make your changes. When finished, select Publish.

You can quickly edit certain parts of a listing with the Editing options tool on Etsy.com. You can also use this tool to edit multiple listings at once. 

  1. Sign in to Etsy.com. 
  2. Go to Shop Manager.
  3. Go to Listings.
  4. Check the box next to each listing you’d like to edit. Check the box at the top of the page to select all listings. 
  5. Go to Editing Options. 
  6. Choose an action from the list.
  7. Make your changes, and then select Apply.

How to edit a listing from your public shop

On your public Etsy.com shop page, you can edit each part of the listing, including the description. 

  1. Sign in to Etsy.com.
  2. On your public shop homepage, select the listing you'd like to edit.
  3. At the top of the listing page, choose Listing Tools.
  4. Select Edit.

How to fix listing search visibility issues 

The following issues may cause your Listings to appear lower in Etsy search results:

  • Having a primary image that’s too dark 
  • Having a primary image that’s low resolution
  • Having a primary image that’s a collage 
  • Having too few images may result in your listing appearing lower in search results. 
  • Lacking a return policy, even if that policy is “no returns accepted” 
  • Lacking a specific category
  • Having a shipping price for US domestic listings higher than 6 dollars. 

  1. From your Shop Manager, go to your Etsy search visibility tab. 
  2. In Your listings, view which issues are affecting your listings’ visibility. Options available may include: Add photos or videos, Replace photo collage, Upload higher-resolution photos, Add return policy, Update Policy, or Offer buyer-friendly US shipping prices.
  3. Choose which issue you want to resolve and select View listings. 
  4. All the listings with the selected issue will be displayed. Edit your listings to correct the search visibility issues.

results.name: How Printed Items From Digital Purchases Work for Sellers
results.title: How Printed Items From Digital Purchases Work for Sellers
results.body:
Etsy is testing a new way for buyers to turn eligible digital files they purchase on Etsy’s website into printed items. If you have eligible digital listings, they may be included in this test automatically. You can opt out if you don’t want your eligible listings to be included.

How does the printed item experience work?

After purchasing an eligible digital file, buyers may see an option to order it as a printed item through a separate checkout on Etsy. Buyers can choose from available options, select the digital file they want to use, preview the item, and place a separate order.

Ventur Editions, a third party print provider, sells and fulfills the printed item from their shop:

  • The printed item has its own listing and reviews.
  • If there’s an issue with the order, Ventur Editions provides support.

Are my listings eligible?

Your digital listings may be included in the test if: 

  • Your shop based in the US or Canada
  • You don't already offer a physical version of the design or use your own print-on-demand integration
  • The file meets the print partner’s requirements for high-quality printing

Can I opt out?

If you don’t want your eligible digital listings included in the test, you can opt out. Once you opt out, the option to order printed items will no longer appear after purchases of your eligible listings. For this test, the opt-out applies to your shop rather than individual listings.

Opting out removes print options from being surfaced after purchases of your eligible listings. It doesn’t prevent buyers from independently accessing Ventur Editions’ services with the content they’ve downloaded. 

To opt out:

  1. On Etsy.com, go to Shop Manager.
  2. Select Settings.
  3. Select Options.
  4. Go to Allow buyers to purchase digital prints and select Disabled.

results.name: How Etsy Funded Coupons Work For Sellers
results.title: How Etsy Funded Coupons Work For Sellers
results.body:
Etsy funds two types of discounts with coupon codes buyers can use during checkout. 

We occasionally publicly promote coupons for use during set dates. We also send coupons privately to buyers for certain occasions. 

Both public and private coupons are fully funded by Etsy, meaning Etsy pays for the discount. The seller receives the full order amount when a buyer uses the coupon code. 

Etsy funded promotions are separate from promo codes a seller can create just for use in their shop.

Etsy funded promotions

Etsy occasionally publicly promotes a coupon code that is active for a set length of time, for example, for 48 hours during a weekend or over a holiday, and in set geographies. Depending on the terms, Buyers may be able to use the coupon as often as they like on qualifying order amounts while it’s active. 

The eligible regions, promotion length, discount amount, and other details may differ depending on the promotion. We often alert sellers about Etsy funded promotions in Forums announcements, Shop Manager cards, and @EtsySuccess on Instagram.

How to participate

As long as you’re enrolled in Etsy Payments you don’t need to do anything more to be eligible.

Here’s how to make the most of these Etsy funded promotions: 

  • Turn on Share & Save. If you make an eligible sale during the promotion through your trackable link, we’ll cover the cost of the promotion and take 4% of the order total (minus the promotional discount) off your Etsy bill.

  • Share your listings on social media and mention the promotion. Go to Listings, choose the gear next to a listing photo, and Share.

  • We often share a special image you can screenshot and share to your own channels. You can typically find these in the Highlights section of the @EtsySuccess Instagram when the promotion goes live.

Terms and Conditions will apply.

Private coupons

Etsy sometimes privately emails coupons to certain buyers that can be applied toward their next eligible Etsy order. Only the recipient can use the coupon and only on one order.

The coupon may be for a fixed-amount discount off eligible orders. These coupons may include special conditions for use, such as a minimum spend requirement. The coupon also includes expiration details on how long the buyer has to use the coupon before it expires. 

Does an Etsy funded coupon change how much I make on a sale or the fees I pay?

These coupons are entirely funded by Etsy. This means that when a buyer uses an Etsy coupon on an order, you still receive the full order amount. After a sale, you can see the full amount on the receipt and reflected in your Payment account.

When a buyer makes a purchase from your shop using an Etsy Coupon, you pay the same seller fees you would have paid on an order without an Etsy Coupon. 

What happens if I issue a refund?

On Etsy.com, when you issue a refund for an order for which a coupon was used, you see a notification of the amount to be refunded to Etsy on the refund confirmation page. 

How do Etsy funded coupons work with taxes? 

Taxes collected and remitted by Etsy

When Etsy is required to pay taxes, Etsy will remit the tax due to the tax authority. Depending on where the buyer is based, Etsy may be required to pay tax on the amount payable by the buyer or on the amount payable before the Etsy coupon is applied. For example, if an item originally costs $100, and the price is $90 after the Etsy discount is applied, taxes will be collected and remitted to eligible governments on either the $100 or the $90 depending on the rules in your country.

Sellers can see when an Etsy funded coupon was used on an order and how much was funded by Etsy in the order details in Shop Manager.

Taxes collected and remitted by sellers

Where you as the seller are required to collect the tax and remit the tax to your local tax authority, the tax treatment depends on your own personal circumstances and the tax rules in your location. To enable you to remit the right amount of taxes, sellers who collect and remit their own taxes can view how much is being funded by Etsy via Etsy Coupons in the order details in their Shop Manager. We recommend that you consult with your tax advisor regarding the amount on which you are required to pay taxes. 

Taxes paid by buyers

For orders where buyers are required to pay taxes, for example where goods are being imported into a particular jurisdiction, local rules will determine whether taxes are charged on the order amount minus the Etsy-funded amount or the order amount before the discount is applied. 

Learn more about taxes for orders shipping internationally.

results.name: How to Customize Your Pattern Site with the Website Editor
results.title: How to Customize Your Pattern Site with the Website Editor
results.body:
The website editor is where you’ll customize the design and content on your website. We’ll go over how to add new pages to your website, manage existing pages, and choose themes that work best with your inventory.

Managing pages

Open all page options for your website by clicking Pages in the lower right corner of the website editor.

The Pages section includes Home, About, Contact Us, Events, and Gallery pages. All of these pages are optional (except your Home page) and can be easily added or removed from your site.

To remove a page from your site, hover over an individual page in the sidebar and select the gear icon. Click Hide page to remove it temporarily from your site. To permanently remove the page and its content, click Delete.

The website editor will display a preview of your website in the main panel. You can edit content directly from this preview.

Home

The Home page is the main page of your website, and the only page you cannot disable. From here, you have the option to edit your site name, cover photo, or shop icon by clicking the pencil icon within each field.

About

The About page is an optional page where you can tell the story of your business. If you frequently share your Pattern site via social media, those sites will usually display your first About image.

Note: If you’re adding or changing About photos for your site, we recommend they be at least 1440 x 800 pixels.

You’re welcome to make changes to your About page or completely remove it from your site. Click the gear icon on the sidebar to hide or remove it.

Contact Us

The Contact Us page is a way for you to share your brand’s contact information with buyers.

We'll display a preview of the contact form that buyers will use to send you a message. You can fill out any combination of these contact options:

  • Retail store location

  • Business hours

  • Phone number

  • Email address

  • Social media links

If you only want to display the contact form, leave all other fields blank.

As you add content to different sections, click the checkmark within each field to save your changes. To see how your contact information appears on your site, select Preview.

If you choose to hide this information, we’ll save any content currently on this page while keeping it hidden from buyers. If you delete this page, no information will be saved.

If you decide not to make this page public, there will still be a Contact Us link at the bottom of the site so visitors can get in touch with you.

Events

This page is where you inform buyers about any events you’re participating in or organizing for your business. You could also use this to promote sales or new product launches. The event doesn’t have to be in-person.

You can customize the name of certain fields on this page by using the in-line editor. Click the checkmark to save your changes.

To create an event:

  1. Click Add event.

  2. Complete the fields in the overlay to provide a date, time, description, location, photos, and any helpful links related to the event.

  3. Select Publish to make your event page live.

For past events, once the date or time of an event passes, the event will be moved to the Past Events section. You can delete the event afterward if you don’t want it displayed here.

Gallery

The Gallery page is where you can post photos that inspire your work or give buyers a closer look at your creative process. Show custom pieces you’ve created in the past, photos of your workspace, or any images that are a source of inspiration for your work.

To add images to your gallery, click Add images. You can add up to 50 photos with captions. If you need to rearrange them, click and drag an image in the overlay,

You can also customize the Gallery page’s title and subheading by clicking into each of the fields. Select the checkmark to save your changes.

Customizing your site's design

The Design section of your Pattern Dashboard, allows you to edit your site's:

  • Primary and secondary fonts

  • Background and accent colors

  • Theme

  • Branding

  • Cart style

  • Listing page gallery photo layout

  • Search bar option
  • Reviews option

Any changes you make on the Design page will automatically display in the preview pane. If you do not wish to save the edits you’ve made, click Back and Clear changes and continue.

Be sure to publish your changes to make them live on your site.

Fonts

Click the Headline dropdown menu to select a primary font for your site. This will set the primary heading font across your Pattern site, including your site title, category headings, and listing titles on product pages.

Click the Body dropdown menu to select a secondary font for your site. This font is used for the navigation bar, cart buttons, listing descriptions, footer links, and other areas of your site.

Background color

Use the Background color dropdown menu to change the background of your Pattern site. You'll see a palette of recommended color options. Select any of the preset options, or click the color wheel on the right to open up a full color chart to set a custom color or enter a specific color code.

Accent and button color

Click the Accent & button color dropdown menu to change the color of the buttons and accents on your site. The Accent & button color presets will change depending on what color you select as a background color. Select any of the preset color options, or click on the color wheel on the right to open up a full color chart to set a custom color or enter a specific color code.

Note: Depending on the theme you’re using, you may need to click on a product image in your preview pane to see the accent color you’ve chosen.

Theme

This is where you’ll customize the layout of your website and inventory. Select from a variety of themes that highlight your featured items, shop sections, and About page. Learn more about your theme options here.

Brand

Click the Brand box to select how you’d like your branding to be displayed on your website. You can display your site name, shop icon, or both. To customize content for each of these fields, click into the appropriate field and make changes directly on the page. Click the checkmark to save your changes.

Note: Any updates you make to your Pattern site won't affect your Etsy shop. If you need to make changes to your Etsy shop, visit Etsy.com.

Cart style

Use the Cart style dropdown menu to choose a cart display option for your website.

  • Dropdown opens up a small box underneath the Cart button at the top of the screen.

  • Slide out opens up an overlay on the right side of the screen.

  • Overlay opens up a window in the center of the screen.

All cart styles give buyers the option to proceed to Checkout, or to continue shopping.

Listing page layout

The Listing page dropdown menu shows options for the way gallery photos are displayed on a listing page.

  • Stacked photos displays all your listing photos on the page at once, one on top of the other.

  • Photo gallery displays the primary listing photo, with the ability to sideways scroll through the other photos.

You can also click on a photo to open a gallery slideshow, which displays the images at a larger size.

Search bar option

Click the Search box to turn search functionality on or off for your Pattern site. When turned on, visitors can use the search box to look for specific items on your site. When turned off, visitors can browse your products from the homepage or shop section navigation.

Reviews
When turned on, visitors can see buyer reviews for listings purchased via Etsy. Reviews will show only on listing pages. Each listing will show only reviews for that corresponding listing on Etsy.com.

Note: Buyers who purchase from your Pattern site are unable to leave reviews at this time.

results.name: Why Was My Listing Removed by Etsy?
results.title: Why Was My Listing Removed by Etsy?
results.body:
The Policy violations page can help you keep track of removed listings, understand why a listing was removed, and get quick access to policy resources right when you need it. In some cases, you may be able to submit an appeal to get your removed listing reinstated.

Listings may be inactive if they expire or sell out, or if you deactivate them.

Learn more about inactive listings.

Listings may also be inactive if your shop is suspended. Many causes of a suspension can be quickly resolved on your own, or by working with our team to resolve the issue. Learn what to do when your account is suspended.

Also, to ensure our members have safe and positive experiences in our marketplace, we may remove listings that we have reason to believe may violate our policies.

Etsy may remove listings that violate the following policies: 

  • Etsy’s Creativity Standards
  • Prohibited Items Policy
  • Sanctions Policy 
  • Intellectual Property Policy

In addition to our policies, items listed on Etsy are required to comply with all applicable laws.

If your listing was removed by Etsy, check your email inbox for a message regarding the removal of your listings. If your listing was removed and you believe this is a mistake, you may be able to appeal to restore it from the Policy violations page. We’re working on making listing appeals available for more policies and more sellers in the future. Learn how listing appeals work.

If you have further questions, please see our Seller Policy for more information on the types of items allowed in our marketplace.

View your removed listings.

My listing contains mature content

While Etsy supports sellers' creative freedom and personal expression, we want to keep our marketplace appropriate for a general audience.

If your listing was removed for mature content that violates our policy, the quickest way to resolve this is to create a new listing that follows our Listing Mature Content Correctly policy and Adult Nudity and Sexual Content policy. 

Per our Adult Nudity and Sexual Content and Listing Mature Content Correctly policies, some types of adult nudity and sexual imagery are permitted on Etsy, but must be obscured in order to be presented appropriately.

This means:

  • Your first listing image should be family-friendly. Mature content must be entirely removed, obscured, or cropped so that it isn’t visible in the thumbnails of your first photos.
  • Subsequent images may show the content unobscured, as long as it is in line with the policies.

results.name: Your Bio and Profile Picture
results.title: Your Bio and Profile Picture
results.body:
Use your bio to introduce yourself to shoppers and other sellers in the Etsy community. Make your bio personal by describing things about yourself and your business. You can add your interests, crafts, hobbies, and other fun things about you. 

Bios are where all members can share details about themselves. If you're a seller, you can add information about your business in your shop's About section. 

To enter your bio:

  1. On Etsy.com, go to Your account.
  2. Go to Account settings.
  3. Go to Edit profile. 
  4. Enter your bio into the About field.
  5. When you’re done, seelct Save changes.

If you have more than one Etsy account, you must list all of them in the Public Profile section of each account.

Learn more about crafting an engaging profile. 

How to upload a profile picture

To upload a profile picture:

  1. On Etsy.com, go to Your account.
  2. Go to Account settings.
  3. Go to Public profile. 
  4. Choose Browse or Choose file to locate the image file on your computer.
  5. Select an image to use. 
  6. Select Save Changes.  

Profile Picture Tips

  • The image you use must be at least 400 x 400 pixels in size and smaller than 10MB. 
  • Make sure your original image is a square, or your profile picture will be distorted on the site. 
  • You can't delete your profile picture, but you can always replace it with a new one. 
  • Profile pictures should be a .jpg, .png, or .gif file only.

How to add your Etsy shop to your profile

To add your shop to your public profile:

  1. On Etsy.com, go to Your account.
  2. Go to Account settings.
  3. Go to Public profile. 
  4. Under Include on Your Profile, check Shop.
  5. Select Save Changes.

results.name: How to Use Attributes When Listing an Item
results.title: How to Use Attributes When Listing an Item
results.body:
Listing attributes allow you to describe your items with distinct, detailed characteristics to help buyers get a clear idea of what you’re selling. Attributes can also help buyers find your items more easily in search results. Learn more about attributes in search. 

How to choose attributes for your listing

When you create a new listing on Etsy, the option to add attributes appears after the item’s categories are chosen. The category you select for your items determines the attributes you can add for the item.

Choose the available attributes that best describe your item so buyers can better understand what you’re selling.

  1. Go to your Shop Manager and select Listings.
  2. Create a new listing or select the listing you want to edit. 
  3. Choose the category that best describes your item. 
  4. Under Item options, find Attributes and select the options that best apply to your listing. 
  5. Select Publish when finished.

  1. Go to Listings. 
  2. Create a new listing or choose the listing you want to edit. 
  3. Select the Listing tab. 
  4. Select Add attributes and select the options that best apply to your listing.
  5. Select Save. 

To remove an attribute from a listing, select the pencil icon and deselect the attribute, then select Save.

What if an attribute doesn't offer an option that I need for my listing?

If you can’t find an exact match for your item, select the most relevant attributes available. Fill out both  attributes and tags for your listings to make sure potential buyers find and see your items on Etsy.

For instance, let’s say you’re listing a handmade, lemon-colored scarf. However, the color “lemon” isn’t a selectable option for the Color attribute.

  • Choose the color that you think would be the closest to lemon. You can select “Yellow” as your option for the Color attribute.
  • If you find that your unique color label is an important search term as well, you can add "lemon scarf" as a listing tag for your item.

Using Materials and Material features

Materials identify substances or components used to make an item, such as Hemp, Organic cotton, or Recycled glass. Material features describe certain characteristics of an item or the materials used to make it, such as Plastic-free, Reusable, Upcycled, or Vegan.

Select an optional Material or Material feature when it accurately describes your item and you have information supporting the selection. By selecting a Material or Material feature, you are making a claim that it accurately describes your item, is not misleading, and is supported by sufficient information. Review the descriptions below to understand what each value means and when to use it.

Materials 

Select a Material when it describes the item’s composition as a whole, rather than only a separate component. Small functional components, such as zippers, buttons, or clasps, may be made from another material when buyers would not ordinarily expect the selected Material to describe them.

Select Hemp or Linen when it makes up the item’s entire fiber composition. Provide the item’s complete fiber composition in the listing description. Selecting Hemp or Linen does not replace any fiber-content or labeling information required under applicable laws.

  • Hemp: refers to textile fiber obtained from the bast of the Cannabis sativa plant. Do not select Hemp for an unrelated fiber that includes “hemp” in its common name, such as Manila hemp, which is abaca.
  • Linen: refers to textile material made from fiber obtained from the bast of the flax plant, Linum usitatissimum.

Select an Organic Material when it makes up the item’s entire fiber composition and you have evidence that the crop was certified to an organic standard recognized under applicable laws. Provide clear details supporting the claim, including the item’s complete fiber composition, in the listing description. Selecting an Organic Material does not replace any fiber-content or labeling information required under applicable laws. 

  • Organic Cotton: refers to cotton fiber from cotton grown and certified to an organic standard recognized under applicable laws.
  • Organic Hemp: refers to textile fiber obtained from the bast of hemp plants (Cannabis sativa) grown and certified to an organic standard recognized under applicable laws.
  • Organic Linen: refers to textile material made from fiber obtained from the bast of flax plants (Linum usitatissimum) grown and certified to an organic standard recognized under applicable laws. 

Select a Recycled material when it makes up the item’s entire fiber or material composition and you have evidence supporting its recycled content. Provide clear details of what is meant by “recycled,” including the item’s complete fiber or material composition, in the listing description. Material routinely reused within the same manufacturing process does not qualify. An existing item or material that is merely reused, repurposed, or incorporated into a new item without being reprocessed into new material also does not qualify as Recycled, although the Upcycled value may be appropriate. Selecting Recycled cotton or Recycled polyester does not replace any fiber-content or labeling information required under applicable laws.

  • Recycled cotton: refers to cotton fiber produced from cotton material recovered or diverted from the waste stream before or after consumer use and reprocessed for use in a new material or product.
  • Recycled polyester: refers to polyester fiber produced from polyester material recovered or diverted from the waste stream before or after consumer use and reprocessed for use in a new material or product.
  • Recycled glass: refers to glass produced from glass material recovered or diverted from the waste stream before or after consumer use and reprocessed for use in a new material or product.
  • Recycled metal: refers to metal produced from metal material recovered or diverted from the waste stream before or after consumer use and reprocessed for use in a new material or product. Identify the type of metal in the listing description (e.g., aluminum, steel, or silver).
  • Recycled paper: refers to paper produced from paper material recovered or diverted from the waste stream before or after consumer use and reprocessed for use in a new material or product. Any recycled-content claim in the listing description must reflect the Recycled paper physically present in the item; do not present a credit-based or allocated claim as physical recycled content.
  • Recycled plastic: refers to plastic produced from plastic material recovered or diverted from the waste stream before or after consumer use and reprocessed for use in a new material or product. Identify the type of plastic in the listing description when that information is available (e.g., PET, HDPE, or polypropylene). Any recycled-content claim in the listing description must reflect the Recycled plastic physically present in the item; do not present a mass-balance or attributed-content claim as physical recycled content.

Material features

Material features describe certain characteristics of an item or the materials used to make it.

Plastic-free: refers to the entire item and its product packaging containing no plastic, including plastic components, coatings, or linings. Conventional, bio-based, biodegradable, and compostable plastics all count as plastic. Select Plastic-free when both the item and its product packaging meet these requirements; an item sold without product packaging may qualify based on the item alone. Do not select Plastic-free if applicable law already requires that type of item to be plastic-free, if plastic would not ordinarily be associated with the item or its product packaging, or if a replacement substance poses the same or similar environmental risks. Packaging used only to ship the order is outside the scope of this value.

Reusable: refers to an item or an identified part of it that is designed to be used multiple times for the same intended purpose and to remain functional under normally expected conditions of use. Select Reusable when the item or identified part is intended to replace a comparable product that is commonly used once and discarded; an ordinary durable item does not qualify merely because it can be used more than once. Identify what is reusable in the listing description, explain how it can be reused, and provide any relevant cleaning, maintenance, or refill instructions. 

Upcycled: refers to an item or an identified part of it created by meaningfully transforming a used, discarded, or surplus product, material, or part into a new or significantly modified item. Upcycling is typically associated with giving an existing product or material a new or improved use, quality, or value. Do not select Upcycled solely because an item was resold, cleaned, repaired, or reused without meaningful transformation. Identify the original input in the listing description, explain how it was transformed, and state whether the value applies to the entire item or one part.

Vegan: refers to an item made without animal-derived ingredients, materials, components, derivatives, or processing aids. Select Vegan when this is true for the entire item and animal-derived inputs may ordinarily be relevant to that type of item. Vegan does not necessarily mean that the item is cruelty-free, was not tested on animals, or is allergen-free. 

What to include in your listing description 

If you select a Material or Material feature, provide enough information in the listing description for buyers to understand how it applies to the item. This may include the item’s material or fiber composition, how a feature applies, or the part of the item the feature describes. Include any additional information identified in the guidance above, and make sure the listing description is accurate and consistent with the attribute you selected.

How to support your selections

Keep records supporting any Material or Material feature you select and any related claims in your listing description. The documentation you need may depend on the item, the claim, and the laws that apply to you. If you refer to a certification, make sure it covers what you describe as certified and retain the supporting documentation.
